query: What happens if the grizzly fails or arch formation occurs in a track hopper?

Query: What happens if the grizzly fails or arch formation occurs in a track hopper?

This draft is based mainly on retrieved course text/image evidence; no supporting relation trace was retrieved.

Key course evidence:
- The Track Hopper area looks quiet between unloadings. Is it safe to approach the grizzly edge? A Yes — if no wagon is on the track, it is safe B Yes — the feeder stops automatically between unloading cycles C No — feeder may still run, arch could collapse, bars may be wet, dust may be present underground D Yes, but only briefly and with both hands free [The Track Hopper area looks quiet between unloadings. Is it safe to approach the grizzly edge?, concept: the-track-hopper-area-looks-quiet-between-unloadings-is-it-safe-to-approach-the-grizzly-edge]
- What is "arch formation" and why is it dangerous? A The hopper structure is arch-shaped for strength B A safety gate that closes the hopper outlet C Coal particles bridge the outlet, stopping flow — then collapse suddenly in a dangerous surge D Coal piling up above ground level during overfill [What is "arch formation" and why is it dangerous?, concept: what-is-arch-formation-and-why-is-it-dangerous]
- What happens if the grizzly fails? 🚨 Chain of Destruction 🪨 Boulder/large lump — destroys feeder belt or apron chain completely 🔩 Metal debris (bolts, wire) — cuts conveyor belt downstream 🌿 Rope or wood — wraps around feeder shaft, causes jam and stall 🪨 Shale/stone — jams between apron plates, cracking the steel pans ⚠ Rule [What happens if the grizzly fails?, concept: what-happens-if-the-grizzly-fails]
- What is the fundamental principle of a Track Hopper? A The wagon is physically rotated to empty coal B Bottom doors open and coal falls by gravity into pit below C A vacuum system draws coal out of the wagon D Hydraulic rams tilt the wagon sideways [What is the fundamental principle of a Track Hopper?, concept: what-is-the-fundamental-principle-of-a-track-hopper]
- What is a Track Hopper? COAL WAGON bottom doors open ⬇⬇⬇ coal accumulating Track Hopper Pit (underground) Rail wagon with open bottom doors discharging coal by gravity into underground hopper A Track Hopper is an underground pit built beneath a rail track. Wagons with bottom-opening doors drive over it — coal falls straight through into the pit below. No tipping. No rotation. Just gravity. [What is a Track Hopper?, concept: what-is-a-track-hopper]

[Arch Formation — The Silent Stop, concept: arch-formation-the-silent-stop]
- Diagram under: The Grizzly — first line of defence. Caption: Steel bar grid — small coal passes, oversized material and debris are stopped. Visible labels: gap; 200–300mm; Fine coal ✓ passes; LARGE; LUMP; ⛔ STOPPED; GRIZZLY SCREEN — Top View; ↓ Fine coal falls freely into hopper pit below. Context: What is a Track Hopper? / Track_Hopper_iCard_Microlearning.html. [The Grizzly — first line of defence, concept: the-grizzly-first-line-of-defence]
